interpretation: The normal public entry reaches GNU before Node or preflight. Default public, JS, private Bash, offline-package and actual Pi checks use no rg searches; only exact experimental flag1 enables the separately qualified semantic routes.

No automatically translated command class has a universal wall-time guarantee. Every such class therefore remains GNU by default; compatibility equality and a real engine invocation do not establish a speed win.
Each environment replays the same generated corpus; repetitions do not increase unique-case coverage.
Actual contributing rg search is distinct from GNU compile checks, Unicode scalar calibration, candidate-only GNU span evaluation, original-command fallback and zero-search routes.

The 18,745 generated CLI cases compare complete stdout/stderr/status. The 5,840 qualified matcher cases independently compare rg matching with GNU; 359 additionally check JSON formatting. The 6,160 native-routing cases check the GNU oracle and dispatch boundary rather than another full wrapper CLI subprocess.
The earlier 30,796-case aggregate included 51 named presentation cases. New minimized regressions are reported separately and do not inflate generated-case counts.
No failures or skips were accepted. Preserved failed matrix/subset and delimiter-color witnesses were repaired without deleting the original generated cases or mismatch assertions.
No universal rg acceleration or speedup is claimed. Compatibility still requires genuine native routes, including unqualified stdin early exits, binary policies and nontrivial collation.

Completed qualified regular-stdin -m searches compare shared descriptor offset and unread-tail bytes as well as output/status. Positional feeding avoids full-suffix spooling; arbitrary concurrent cursor changes and interrupted native read-ahead equivalence are not proved.
This record was written after capture and identifies the immutable tested archive and current implementation/test hashes, not a self-referential tarball containing its own hash.

The previously preserved VM oracle EPIPE was a test-harness failure feeding unused stdin to file-only GNU searches. File-only cases now receive no payload, genuine stdin cases still do, and execution errors remain fatal. No comparison cases or mismatch assertions were deleted.
